title: Meeting someone
goal: Introduce yourself, say where you are from, and keep the conversation going.

turns.prompt: Say hello and give your name: My name is Ana.
turns.note: Me llamo literally means “I call myself.” Soy Ana is also a natural introduction.

turns.prompt: Say: Nice to meet you too.
turns.note: Mucho gusto is a simple, widely understood reply.

turns.prompt: Say: I’m from Canada.
turns.note: Use ser de to say where you are from.

turns.prompt: Say: I work in a hotel.
turns.note: Trabajo is the present-tense yo form of trabajar.

turns.prompt: Say: A little. I’m learning.
turns.note: Estoy aprendiendo describes what you are doing right now.

title: At a café
goal: Order politely, ask for the bill, and understand a common question.

turns.prompt: Order a coffee with milk, please.
turns.answer: Un café con leche, por favor.
turns.note: Por favor makes the order polite. In Spain, café con leche is a common order.

turns.prompt: Say: Nothing else, thank you.
turns.note: Nada más means “nothing more.”

turns.prompt: Say: To have here, please.
turns.note: Para llevar means “to go / takeaway.”

turns.prompt: Ask: How much is it?
turns.note: Listen for cuánto with its accent: it is a question word.

turns.prompt: Say: Thank you. See you later.
turns.note: Hasta luego is a friendly everyday goodbye.

title: At a restaurant
setting: Getting a table and ordering dinner
goal: Ask for a table, order food, and request the check.

turns.prompt: Say: No, we don’t have a reservation.
turns.meaning: No, we don’t have a reservation.
turns.note: Spanish commonly repeats no: one before the verb and one in the reply.

turns.prompt: Say: A table for two, please.
turns.answer: Una mesa para dos, por favor.
turns.note: Mesa is feminine, so use una.

turns.prompt: Say: I’d like the fish, please.
alternatives: Me gustaría el pescado, por favor.
turns.note: Quisiera is a polite way to say “I would like.”

turns.prompt: Say: Water, without ice, please.
alternatives: Quiero agua sin hielo, por favor.
turns.note: Agua is feminine, but takes el in the singular: el agua fría.

turns.prompt: Ask for the bill, please.
turns.note: La cuenta is the bill/check. In Spain, it is not usually called factura at a restaurant.

title: Finding your way
goal: Ask where a place is and follow simple directions.

turns.prompt: Ask politely: Where is the train station?
turns.note: Use estar for the location of a specific place.

turns.prompt: Ask: Is it far?
turns.meaning: Is it far? / Is it very far?
turns.note: Lejos means “far”; cerca means “near.”

turns.prompt: Check: Do I go straight ahead?
turns.note: Todo recto is a common way to say “straight ahead.”

turns.partner: Sí, y luego gire a la izquierda.
turns.prompt: Ask: Is it on the left?
turns.note: A la izquierda means “on the left”; a la derecha means “on the right.”

turns.prompt: Say: Thank you for your help.
turns.note: Gracias por is followed by a noun or an infinitive: gracias por ayudarme.

title: At the market
goal: Ask for an amount, check the price, and pay naturally.

turns.prompt: Ask for a kilo of apples, please.
turns.answer: Un kilo de manzanas, por favor.
turns.note: After a quantity, Spanish often uses de: un kilo de…

turns.prompt: Say: Half a kilo of oranges.
turns.note: Medio agrees with the masculine kilo.

turns.prompt: Say: No, thank you. I have a bag.
turns.meaning: No, thank you. I have a bag.
turns.note: Tengo is the irregular yo form of tener.

turns.prompt: Ask: Can I pay by card?
turns.note: Puedo is the yo form of poder: o changes to ue.

turns.prompt: Say: Perfect. Here you are.
turns.note: Aquí tiene is a polite way to hand something to someone.

title: Checking into a hotel
goal: Check in, give your name, and ask about breakfast and Wi-Fi.

turns.prompt: Say: I have a reservation.
alternatives: Tengo una reserva a mi nombre.
turns.note: Tener means “to have”; its yo form is tengo.

turns.prompt: Say: It’s under the name Novak.
alternatives: La reserva está a nombre de Novak.
turns.note: A nombre de is the standard phrase for a booking under someone’s name.

turns.prompt: Say: Of course. Here it is.
turns.note: Lo refers to the masculine passport: el pasaporte.

turns.partner: El desayuno es de siete a diez.
turns.prompt: Ask: Is breakfast included?
turns.note: Incluido agrees with desayuno, which is masculine.

turns.partner: Sí. La clave del wifi está en la habitación.
turns.prompt: Ask: What is the Wi-Fi password?
turns.note: Cuál es asks for a specific piece of information.

title: Taking the train
goal: Buy a ticket, ask about the platform, and confirm the time.

turns.prompt: Say: I’m going to Seville.
turns.note: Voy is the yo form of ir.

turns.prompt: Say: A return ticket, please.
turns.note: Ida y vuelta means “there and back.”

turns.prompt: Say: At ten in the morning.
turns.answer: A las diez de la mañana.
turns.note: Use a la with one o’clock and a las with other hours.

turns.partner: El tren sale del andén cuatro.
turns.prompt: Ask: Which platform did you say?
turns.note: Andén means “platform.” Asking again is a useful real-world skill.

turns.prompt: Say: Thank you. Have a good day.
turns.answer: Gracias. Que tenga un buen día.
turns.meaning: Thank you. Have a good day.
turns.note: Que tenga is a polite wish using the subjunctive; igualmente means “you too.”

title: When you don’t understand
goal: Ask someone to repeat, slow down, or explain a word.

turns.prompt: Say: Sorry, I don’t understand.
turns.note: No goes directly before the verb entiendo.

turns.prompt: Ask: Can you repeat that, please?
turns.note: Puede is polite; puedes is informal. The lo in repetirlo means “it.”

turns.prompt: Ask: Can you speak more slowly?
turns.note: Más despacio means “more slowly.”

turns.prompt: Say: I understand now, thank you.
turns.note: Ahora means “now”; ya can mean “now” or “already.”

turns.prompt: Ask: What does “despacio” mean?
turns.note: ¿Qué significa…? is a handy way to ask what a word means.

title: Making plans with a friend
goal: Accept an invitation, agree on a time and place, and say goodbye.

turns.prompt: Say: Nothing special. Why?
turns.note: Por qué (two words, accent) asks why; porque (one word) means because.

turns.prompt: Say: Yes, I would love to!
turns.note: Me encantaría (I would love to) sounds warmer than a plain sí.

turns.prompt: Suggest: At seven?
turns.note: Quedar means to arrange to meet. Times use la/las: a la una, a las siete.

turns.prompt: Say: In front of the cinema.
turns.note: de + el always contracts to del.

turns.prompt: Say: See you!
turns.note: Nos vemos (literally “we see each other”) is a friendly everyday goodbye.

title: Small talk with a neighbour
goal: Talk about the weather, work, and your weekend.

turns.prompt: Agree: Yes, it is very hot.
turns.note: Weather uses hacer: hace calor, hace frío, hace sol.

turns.prompt: Say: Fine, but I am very busy.
turns.meaning: Fine, but I am very busy.
turns.note: Estar ocupado/a means to be busy: a temporary state, so estar.

turns.partner: ¿Y qué hiciste el fin de semana?
turns.prompt: Say: I went to the beach with my family.
turns.answer: Fui a la playa con mi familia.
turns.meaning: I went to the beach with my family.
turns.note: Fui is the preterite of ir — and of ser. Context tells you which.

turns.prompt: Say: It was a bit cold.
turns.note: The imperfect estaba describes how something was. Fría agrees with el agua, which is feminine.

turns.partner: Bueno, me voy. ¡Que tengas un buen día!
turns.prompt: Say: Same to you!
turns.note: Igualmente is the easiest reply to any good wish.

title: At the pharmacy
goal: Describe a simple symptom, answer questions, and understand instructions.

turns.prompt: Say: I have a headache.
turns.note: Doler works like gustar: me duele + the body part with la/el, not mi.

turns.prompt: Say: Since yesterday.
turns.note: ¿Desde cuándo…? asks how long something has been going on.

turns.prompt: Say: No, but I am very tired.
turns.meaning: No, but I am very tired.
turns.note: Use cansada if you are a woman. Tired is a state, so estar.

turns.partner: Tome una pastilla cada ocho horas.
turns.prompt: Ask: Do I take it with food?
turns.meaning: Do I take it with food?
turns.note: La replaces la pastilla and goes before the verb.

turns.prompt: Say: Thanks. How much is it?
turns.note: ¿Cuánto es? asks for the total you have to pay.

title: Buying clothes
goal: Browse, ask for a size, try something on, and buy it.

turns.prompt: Say: I am just looking, thanks.
turns.note: The standard way to tell a shop assistant you are browsing.

turns.partner: Muy bien. Si necesita algo, me dice.
turns.prompt: Ask: Do you have this shirt in a medium?
turns.answer: ¿Tiene esta camisa en la talla mediana?
alternatives: ¿Tiene esta camisa en la talla M?
turns.meaning: Do you have this shirt in a medium?
turns.note: Talla is the size of clothes; for shoes say número.

turns.prompt: Ask: Can I try it on?
turns.note: Probarse means to try on. La refers to la camisa.

turns.partner: Claro, los probadores están al fondo. ¿Qué tal le queda?
turns.prompt: Say: It is a bit big.
turns.meaning: It is a bit big (on me).
turns.note: Quedar describes fit: me queda bien, grande, pequeña.

turns.partner: Aquí tiene una talla más pequeña. ¿Mejor?
turns.prompt: Say: Yes, perfect. I will take it.
turns.meaning: Yes, perfect. I will take it.
turns.note: Me lo/la llevo (I will take it) is the natural phrase when you decide to buy.

title: Taking a taxi
goal: Give a destination, ask how long it takes, and pay.

turns.prompt: Say: To the airport, please.
turns.note: a + el always contracts to al.

turns.prompt: Say: Terminal two.
turns.note: Terminal is feminine: la terminal.

turns.partner: Muy bien. Hay bastante tráfico hoy.
turns.prompt: Ask: How long will it take?
turns.note: Tardar means to take time.

turns.prompt: Ask: Can I pay by card?
turns.note: Pagar con tarjeta = by card; en efectivo = in cash.

turns.partner: Sí, claro. Ya hemos llegado. Son treinta euros.
turns.prompt: Say: Here you are. Keep the change.
turns.answer: Aquí tiene. Quédese con el cambio.
turns.meaning: Here you are. Keep the change.
turns.note: Quédese is the polite (usted) command of quedarse.

title: At the doctor’s
goal: Explain how long you have been ill, mention an allergy, and ask a follow-up question.

turns.prompt: Say: I have had a cough for three days.
turns.answer: Tengo tos desde hace tres días.
turns.meaning: I have had a cough for three days.
turns.note: Present tense + desde hace + time = something that started in the past and is still going on.

turns.prompt: Say: Yes, a lot, especially at night.
turns.answer: Sí, mucho, sobre todo por la noche.
alternatives: Sí, mucho, especialmente por la noche.
turns.meaning: Yes, a lot, especially at night.
turns.note: Por la noche = at night; sobre todo = especially.

turns.prompt: Say: Yes, to penicillin.
alternatives: Sí, soy alérgico a la penicilina.
Sí, soy alérgica a la penicilina.
turns.note: Ser alérgico/a a… = to be allergic to…

turns.partner: Bien. Le voy a recetar un jarabe.
turns.prompt: Ask: Do I have to come back?
turns.meaning: Do I have to come back?
turns.note: Tener que + infinitive = to have to.

turns.partner: Solo si no mejora en una semana.
turns.prompt: Say: Understood. Thank you very much.
turns.note: Entendido, de acuerdo and vale all confirm that you understood.

title: Booking a table by phone
goal: Make a reservation: day, number of people, time, and name.

turns.prompt: Say: Hello, I would like to book a table.
alternatives: Hola, me gustaría reservar una mesa.
turns.meaning: Hello, I would like to book a table.
turns.note: Quería (imperfect) sounds softer and more polite than quiero.

turns.prompt: Say: For tomorrow night.
turns.note: Mañana por la noche = tomorrow night; mañana por la mañana = tomorrow morning.

turns.prompt: Say: For four people.
turns.note: Para introduces who or when the booking is for.

turns.prompt: Say: At nine, if possible.
turns.answer: A las nueve, si es posible.
alternatives: A las nueve, si puede ser.
turns.note: Si es posible / si puede ser make a request softer.

turns.prompt: Say: Under the name Martín.
turns.note: A nombre de… = under the name of…

title: Checking in at the airport
goal: Hand over documents, check a bag, choose a seat, and ask about boarding.

turns.partner: Buenos días. Su pasaporte, por favor.
turns.prompt: Say: Here you are.
turns.note: Aquí tiene is what you say when handing something over.

turns.prompt: Say: Yes, one suitcase.
turns.note: Facturar = to check in luggage; equipaje de mano = hand luggage.

turns.prompt: Say: Window, please.
turns.note: Ventanilla is the window seat; pasillo is the aisle.

turns.partner: Su vuelo sale por la puerta doce.
turns.prompt: Ask: What time does boarding start?
turns.note: Embarque = boarding; embarcar = to board.

turns.partner: A las diez y media. ¡Buen viaje!
turns.prompt: Say: Thank you, have a good day.
turns.answer: Gracias, que tenga un buen día.
turns.meaning: Thank you, have a good day.
turns.note: Que tenga… uses the subjunctive — learn it as a fixed polite wish.
